cards.name: hamming_weight_phasing_shared_angle_layers
cards.identity: Let R_1..R_k be k rotations about Pauli axes P_1..P_k that (a) all have the SAME Z-angle theta modulo the Clifford part (equal |residue| after stripping pi/4 multiples; opposite signs handled by flipping the corresponding parity bit with an X) and (b) pairwise commute in the circuit frame, so the whole group acts as the diagonal unitary D = prod_j exp(-i theta P_j / 2). Step 1 (frame-to-wire): conjugate by Cliffords/CNOTs so each P_j becomes a single-wire Z on a distinct carrier wire c_j (for a group of independent Z-parities z_a z_b this is the usual cx(a,b); rz; cx(a,b) parity trick, generalized to one CNOT network for the whole group); the group is then rz(theta) applied to k distinct wires c_1..c_k. Step 2 (Hamming-weight phasing): for a basis state x on the carriers with w = sum_j x_j, prod_j rz(theta) acts as e^{-i theta k / 2} * e^{i theta w}. Compute w into an m-qubit weight register, m = ceil(log2(k+1)), in CLEAN ancillas with a tree of full/half adders (each full adder = 2 CNOT + 1 AND/Toffoli; total k - popcount-style cost, k - m ANDs), then apply ONE rotation rz(2^j * theta) to weight bit j for j = 0..m-1, then uncompute the adder tree (AND gates uncomputed by measurement + classically controlled CZ fix-up, 0 T, via the and_compute/and_uncompute gadgets; AND compute costs 4 T). Step 3: undo the Step-1 CNOT network. Net: k synthesized rotations -> m synthesized rotations + (k - m) AND gadgets, carriers and ancillas restored.
cards.correctness: With rz(theta) = diag(e^{-i theta/2}, e^{+i theta/2}), on a computational basis state x of the k carriers prod_{j=1..k} rz(theta)_{c_j} |x> = exp(i theta (2w - k)/2) |x> = e^{-i theta k/2} * e^{i theta w} |x>, where w = sum_j x_j. The factor e^{-i theta k/2} is x-independent, hence an unobservable global phase (invariant 6). Writing w = sum_{j<m} 2^j w_j, e^{i theta w} = prod_j exp(i theta 2^j w_j), which is exactly the action of diag(1, e^{i theta 2^j}) = rz(2^j theta) (up to another x-independent phase) applied to weight bit w_j. The adder tree is a classical reversible function x -> (w, garbage) on clean |0> ancillas; the rotations are diagonal so they do not disturb it, and running the tree backwards restores all ancillas to |0> for every input, so the construction is a unitary on the data wires equal to D up to global phase. Measurement-based AND uncompute keeps this exactly: the measured branch applies a known Clifford fix-up (CZ) that is classically corrected, so every branch realizes the same operator with the same phase (invariant 2). Step 1/Step 3 conjugation by Cliffords is exact by definition of the Pauli frame; grouping is legitimate because the P_j pairwise commute, so reordering the rotations into a single layer is exact.
cards.trigger: Scan the op list and maintain the Pauli frame (v3.api.pauli.conjugate) so each t/tdg/rz carries an axis P and angle a. Bucket rotations by residue r = ((a mod pi/2) folded into (-pi/4, pi/4]) with the stripped pi/4 multiple emitted separately as a Clifford/T gate. Inside each bucket, greedily take maximal windows of >= 3 rotations such that (i) all residues are equal in absolute value, (ii) their axes pairwise commute (pauli.commutes_with_z style check on the shared frame), (iii) the axes are linearly independent over GF(2) so they can be routed to distinct carriers, and (iv) no non-Clifford op outside the group and no H that changes the frame of a member axis lies between the first and last member. On tfim_6 this fires on the Trotter ZZ-bond layers (axes z_i z_{i+1}, residue 0.5, groups of ~5) and on the transverse-field layers (x_i after the h rz h sandwich, residue 0.015, groups of up to 6). Skip a window if m >= k (no gain).
cards.expected_effect: tfim_6 has 160 rz but only TWO distinct non-Clifford residues: +-0.5 (90 ops at 0.5, 10 at 11.495574 = 3.5pi + 0.5) and +-0.015 (42 at 11.010574 = 3.5pi + 0.015, 9 at 0.015, 9 at 1.555796 = pi/2 - 0.015). Grouping the 0.5-bucket into ~18 bond layers of 5 (5 -> 3 rotations, 2 AND gadgets each) and the 0.015-bucket into ~7 field layers of 6 (6 -> 3 rotations, 3 AND gadgets each) takes N_Rz from 160 to roughly 100-105. Secondary gain: eps_rz = (eps/2)/N_Rz grows as N_Rz falls, so per-rotation gridsynth cost stays near 54 T instead of rising. Cost: ~55 AND gadgets * 4 T = ~220 T, plus a handful of CNOTs and ceil(log2 7) = 3 extra clean ancillas (6 -> 9 qubits). Estimated total: ~103 * 55 + 220 ~= 5900 T vs 8560 T now. Because every one of TKET / pyzx / BQSKit-FT / BQSKit-DPF reports >= 8560 here, the circuit is locally optimal in the no-ancilla, no-measurement class, which is precisely the class this rule leaves.
cards.source: Hamming weight phasing: Gidney & Fowler, 'Efficient magic state factories with a catalyzed |CCZ> to 2|T> transformation', Quantum 3, 135 (2019), App. on phasing many equal-angle rotations; used for Trotterized Hamiltonians in Kivlichan et al., 'Improved fault-tolerant quantum simulation of condensed-phase correlated electrons via Trotterization', Quantum 4, 296 (2020). Measurement-based AND uncompute: Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018).

cards.name: free_fermion_gaussian_resynthesis
cards.identity: Define Majorana operators on n qubits by g_{2j} = (prod_{k<j} Z_k) X_j, g_{2j+1} = (prod_{k<j} Z_k) Y_j (Jordan-Wigner). A unitary U is Gaussian iff U g_a U^dag = sum_b R_{ab} g_b with R in O(2n). Step 1 (normal form): walk the op list once and push every Clifford to the END using the existing Pauli-frame machinery (v3.api.pauli.conjugate), so the circuit becomes exp(-i a_1 P_1/2) ... exp(-i a_m P_m/2) * C, with P_k Paulis in the fixed frame, a_k the Z-angles of the t/tdg/rz ops, and C one residual Clifford (0 T, kept verbatim). Step 2 (quadraticity test): each P_k must be a Majorana bilinear, i.e. P_k = +-i g_a g_b for some a<b; equivalently P_k is, up to sign, one of Z_j (= -i g_{2j} g_{2j+1}) or a JW string of the form A_i (prod_{i<k<j} Z_k) B_j with A,B in {X,Y} (= +-i g_{2i+c} g_{2j+d}). This is a table lookup on the Pauli's support pattern; the rule bails if any P_k fails it. Step 3 (collapse): exp(-i a P/2) with P = -i g_a g_b acts on Majoranas as the plane rotation G(a,b;a_k) (angle a_k in the (a,b) plane of R^{2n}, identity elsewhere). Multiply them in circuit order: R = G_m ... G_1, one 2n x 2n real orthogonal matrix (numpy). Step 4 (resynthesis): decompose R into a Givens/Bogoliubov network of elementary plane rotations in ADJACENT Majorana planes (a, a+1) by the standard Jiang et al. / Kivlichan et al. cascade: repeatedly zero out subdiagonal entries of R with adjacent-plane Givens rotations, giving at most dim SO(2n) = n(2n-1) = 66 angles for n = 6 (plus a possible det R = -1 factor, realized by the single Clifford Majorana g_0 = X_0, free). Step 5 (emit): map each adjacent-plane angle back to its Pauli bilinear and emit it as cx(i,i+1); rz(phi) ; cx(i,i+1) (for the X_iX_{i+1}/Y_iY_{i+1}-type planes, with the usual h/s dressing) or a bare rz(phi) (for the Z_j planes); append C unchanged. Angles phi that land on a multiple of pi/4 are emitted as Clifford/T by with_ops and cost no synthesis.
cards.correctness: Gaussian (matchgate) unitaries form a group with a faithful-up-to-phase homomorphism U -> R in O(2n) given by the adjoint action on the Majorana algebra; the kernel is global phase only (plus the parity sign for det R = -1), which is unobservable (invariant 6). Each Pauli rotation about a Majorana bilinear is Gaussian: exp(i t g_a g_b /2) g_a exp(-i t g_a g_b/2) = cos(t) g_a + sin(t) g_b and fixes every other g_c, i.e. exactly the plane rotation G(a,b;t); this is the standard Bogoliubov generator relation and follows from g_a^2 = 1, {g_a,g_b} = 0. Hence the product of all m rotations maps to the matrix product R = G_m...G_1, and ANY circuit whose Majorana image is R implements the same unitary up to global phase. The Givens cascade is the exact QR-type factorization of an orthogonal matrix into adjacent plane rotations (Jiang et al.), so the re-emitted network has Majorana image R by construction. Step 1 is exact (Clifford conjugation of Pauli rotation axes); the residual Clifford C is carried through untouched, so no assumption about C is needed. Crucially, the TFIM Trotter input IS in this class: with H = sum J Z_iZ_{i+1} + sum h X_i, the global-Hadamard dual XX + Z is quadratic under JW, so every Trotter factor and hence the whole TKET-optimized unitary is Gaussian (the program tests both JW conventions and bails otherwise, so correctness never depends on the guess). The only error is floating point in the orthogonal factorization (operator distance ~1e-12, charged to the approx budget 5e-4, i.e. ~8 orders of magnitude of headroom); residual non-orthogonality is re-projected before emitting.
cards.trigger: Fires on a Clifford+Rz circuit with n <= 20 when, after pushing all Cliffords to the end, EVERY non-Clifford rotation's frame axis P_k is a Majorana bilinear in one of the two JW conventions (direct, or all-qubit-Hadamard-conjugated), and the number of rotations m exceeds n(2n-1). On tfim_6: the 90 rotations at residue 0.5 have axes Z_iZ_{i+1} (or their frame images X_iX_{i+1} after the h-rz-h sandwiches visible in the trigrams 'h rz h', 18x) and the 60 rotations at residue 0.015 have single-qubit axes X_i / Z_i; both patterns are bilinears, and m = 160 > 66, so the rule applies to the whole circuit as one match.
cards.expected_effect: All 160 synthesized rz ops are replaced by at most n(2n-1) = 66 rotations (the dimension of SO(12)), plus O(n^2) CNOTs and the unchanged residual Clifford. Because eps_rz = (eps/2)/N_Rz rises from 6.25e-6 to about 7.6e-6, per-rotation gridsynth cost stays near 52 T, so T goes from 8560 to roughly 66 * 52 = 3400-3900 (allowing some slack for angles the cascade leaves in non-adjacent planes needing a second rotation). No ancillas, no measurement, qubit count stays 6, CNOT count stays comparable. This is invisible to TKET / pyzx / BQSKit-FT / BQSKit-DPF (all report 8560) because they reason with local templates, ZX rewrites and unitary resynthesis on small windows, none of which can see that the whole 675-op circuit is one free-fermion Gaussian unitary with only 66 free parameters; the circuit is locally optimal exactly because the redundancy is global.
cards.source: Jiang, Sung, Kechedzhi, Smelyanskiy, Boixo, 'Quantum algorithms to simulate many-body physics of correlated fermions', Phys. Rev. Applied 9, 044036 (2018) (Givens/Bogoliubov network for a general Gaussian unitary); Kivlichan, McClean, Wiebe, Gidney, Aspuru-Guzik, Chan, Babbush, 'Quantum simulation of electronic structure with linear depth and connectivity', PRL 120, 110501 (2018); Terhal & DiVincenzo, 'Classical simulation of noninteracting-fermion quantum circuits', PRA 65, 032325 (2002) and Jozsa & Miyake, 'Matchgates and classical simulation of quantum circuits', Proc. R. Soc. A 464, 3089 (2008) (matchgate / O(2n) homomorphism).
